related_questions.question: What should I do if I have been exposed to someone with COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: If you've been exposed to someone with COVID-19, take these steps: start wearing a high-quality mask or respirator (like an N95) immediately. Avoid crowded places where you can't mask. Take extra precautions if you're around people more vulnerable to severe illness. Get tested at least 5 days after your last exposure, even if you don't have symptoms. Continue precautions, including masking, for 10 days after exposure.
snippet_highlighted_words: start wearing a high-quality mask or respirator (like an N95) immediately

list.title: Start Precautions Immediately:
list.snippet: Begin wearing a mask and taking other precautions as soon as you learn of the exposure.

list.title: High-Quality Masking:
list.snippet: Opt for a high-quality mask or respirator like an N95, which offers the best protection.

list.title: Avoid Crowded Settings:
list.snippet: Steer clear of locations where you can't wear a mask comfortably and safely.

list.title: Special Considerations:
list.snippet: If you're around individuals at higher risk for severe illness, take extra steps to protect them.

list.title: Testing:
list.snippet: Get tested for COVID-19 at least 5 days after your last exposure. Even if you test negative, continue precautions through day 10.

list.title: Day Count:
list.snippet: Day 0 is the day of your last exposure to the infected person.

related_questions.question: How long do COVID germs stay in the air?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 virus particles can remain airborne for hours, potentially lingering in the air after an infected person has left the space. Studies suggest the virus can stay airborne for up to 3 hours. Factors like ventilation and room size can influence how long the virus remains airborne according to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (.gov).

list.title: Airborne Transmission:
list.snippet: COVID-19 can be spread through the air via small droplets and particles, which can linger in the air for extended periods.

list.title: Duration:
list.snippet: Research indicates that the virus can remain viable in the air for up to 3 hours, according to WebMD.

list.title: Factors Affecting Duration:
list.snippet: Ventilation systems, room size, and the presence of air filtration systems can impact how long the virus stays airborne.

list.title: Persistence:
list.snippet: The virus can be present in the air even after an infected person has left the space.
